questions.question_text: When must a South Dakota broker associate obtain Errors and Omissions insurance?
distractors: Within 30 days after licensure
Within the first renewal period
Only after closing their first transaction
questions.explanation: Proof of coverage must be filed before an active license is issued, again on renewal, and again on reactivation (ARSD 20:69:15:02). Coverage comes through the commission's group plan or a certified independent policy.

questions.question_text: What are the current E&O insurance coverage limits in South Dakota?
distractors: $50,000 per claim / $250,000 aggregate
$250,000 per claim / $1,000,000 aggregate
$500,000 per claim / $2,000,000 aggregate
questions.explanation: The minimum is $100,000 single-limit coverage per claim and a $500,000 annual aggregate per licensee (ARSD 20:69:15:03). The deductible may not exceed one percent of the single limit — $1,000 — with a like amount for defense and investigation.

questions.question_text: A broker associate allows their E&O policy to lapse without obtaining new coverage. What is the consequence?
questions.correct_answer: The license goes inactive until proof of coverage is filed
distractors: A $50 late fee applies until coverage is restored
No consequence if they are not actively selling
An automatic 90-day grace period applies
questions.explanation: The commission places the license on inactive status as of the date coverage terminates, and the licensee must surrender the license and identification card (ARSD 20:69:15:08.01). No licensed activity may resume until proof of insurance is filed.

questions.question_text: Which type of SD licensee is NOT required to carry E&O insurance?
questions.correct_answer: All active licensees must carry E&O insurance
distractors: Residential rental agents are exempt
Property managers with fewer than 10 units
Broker associates in their first year
questions.explanation: Every licensee on active status must carry coverage; only inactive licensees are excused (SDCL 36-21A-119). That takes in brokers, broker associates, property managers, auctioneers, and residential rental agents — there is no small-portfolio or first-year exception.

questions.question_text: The SDREC helps licensees obtain E&O coverage through what mechanism?
distractors: A state-funded insurance pool
Direct reimbursement of premium costs
Mandatory coverage through the Recovery Fund
questions.explanation: The commission bids out a group policy open to every licensee that the insurer may not cancel (SDCL 36-21A-120). A licensee may instead certify independent coverage, and a responsible broker may certify $500,000/$1,000,000 covering all associated licensees.

questions.question_text: Which insurer counts as a "qualified insurance carrier" for South Dakota E&O coverage?
questions.correct_answer: An A.M. Best class VI or higher carrier authorized in South Dakota
distractors: A carrier rated by A.M. Best in any financial size category
A carrier approved by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners
Any carrier licensed to do business in the licensee's home state
questions.explanation: A qualified insurance carrier must carry an A.M. Best financial size category of class VI or higher and be authorized by the South Dakota Division of Insurance to do business in the state (ARSD 20:69:15:01). A strong rating alone does not qualify a carrier.

questions.question_text: May a South Dakota E&O policy exclude claims arising from a licensee's dishonest or fraudulent acts?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, but not against a licensee who did not participate and reported it
distractors: Yes, and the exclusion may be applied to every licensee in the firm
No, dishonest acts must be covered on the same terms as negligence
No, unless the licensee has already been convicted of the underlying act
questions.explanation: A policy may exclude claims arising from criminal, dishonest, fraudulent, or willful acts (ARSD 20:69:15:04(3)). That exclusion may not be applied to an insured who did not personally participate in the act and who reported it upon learning of it.

questions.question_text: A South Dakota E&O policy may exclude claims arising from the management or sale of which property?
questions.correct_answer: Property in which the licensee or spouse holds over 10 percent
distractors: Any property in which the licensee holds an ownership interest at all
Property the licensee acquired through a foreclosure or tax sale
Property listed with a brokerage other than the licensee's own firm
questions.explanation: Coverage may exclude claims arising from the management or sale of property in which the insured or the insured's spouse holds more than a 10 percent financial or ownership interest (ARSD 20:69:15:04(8)). Smaller stakes stay within coverage.

questions.question_text: A responsible broker wants one policy to satisfy the E&O requirement for the whole firm. What coverage must be certified?
distractors: $100,000/$500,000 in the broker's own name
$250,000/$500,000 plus a rider for each associate
A firm policy cannot satisfy individual requirements
questions.explanation: A responsible broker may comply on behalf of the firm by certifying coverage of at least $500,000 per claim and $1,000,000 aggregate, provided every licensee associated with the broker is covered (ARSD 20:69:15:06.01). Otherwise each licensee certifies $100,000/$500,000.

questions.question_text: A licensee who carries independent E&O coverage is replacing the expiring policy. When must the new certification reach the commission?
questions.correct_answer: By 5:00 p.m. on the date the current coverage expires
distractors: Within 10 days after the replacement policy takes effect
By the last business day of the month coverage expires
At the next license renewal, with the renewal application
questions.explanation: Certification of optional independent coverage must reach the commission by 5:00 p.m. on the date the current coverage expires (ARSD 20:69:15:07). A certification filed late leaves the license on inactive status as of that day.
